papers.title: MetagenomicKG: a knowledge graph for metagenomic applications
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The sheer volume and variety of genomic content within microbial communities makes metagenomics a field rich in biomedical knowledge. To traverse these complex communities and their vast unknowns, metagenomic studies often depend on distinct reference databases, such as the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB), the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and the Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center (BV-BRC), for various analytical purposes. These databases are crucial for the genetic and functional annotation of microbial communities. Nevertheless, the inconsistent nomenclature or identifiers of these databases present challenges for effective integration, representation, and utilization. Knowledge graphs (KGs) offer an appropriate solution by organizing biological entities from different databases to standardized identifiers, allowing their interrelations to be captured into a cohesive network regardless of the naming conventions used in each source. The graph structure not only facilitates the unveiling of hidden patterns but also enriches our biological understanding with deeper insights. Despite KGs having shown potential in various biomedical fields, their application in metagenomics remains underexplored. Results We present MetagenomicKG, a novel knowledge graph specifically tailored for metagenomic analysis. MetagenomicKG integrates taxonomic, functional, and pathogenesis-related information on the human microbiome sourced from various databases, and further connects these with existing biomedical KGs to expand the biological network. Through various case studies involving the human microbiome, we demonstrate its utility in enabling hypothesis generation regarding the relationships between microbes and diseases, generating sample-specific graph embeddings, and providing robust pathogen prediction. papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
微生物群落中基因组信息的庞大数量与多样性使得宏基因组学成为了一个蕴含丰富生物医学知识的领域。为了研究这些复杂的微生物群落及其众多未知之处，宏基因组学研究通常需要依赖诸如基因组分类数据库（GTDB）、京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）以及细菌与病毒生物信息资源中心（BV-BRC）等参考数据库来进行各种分析工作。这些数据库对于对微生物群落的遗传特征与功能进行解析至关重要。然而，由于这些数据库在命名规则或标识符方面存在差异，因此它们的数据难以有效整合、呈现及利用。知识图谱通过将来自不同数据库的生物实体统一映射到标准化标识符上，使得这些信息能够被整合成一个连贯的网络结构，从而克服了上述问题。这种图结构不仅有助于揭示隐藏在数据背后的规律，还能帮助我们更深入地理解生物学现象。尽管知识图谱已在多个生物医学领域展现出巨大潜力，但其在宏基因组学中的应用仍亟待进一步探索。  

**结果**  
我们开发了一种专为宏基因组学分析设计的知识图谱工具——MetagenomicKG。该工具整合了来自多种数据库的人类微生物组的分类信息、功能数据以及与致病性相关的信息，并将这些数据与现有的生物医学知识图谱相连，从而构建出一个更为完善的生物学网络。通过多个涉及人类微生物组的案例研究，我们证明了MetagenomicKG在帮助建立微生物与疾病之间关系的假说、生成特定样本的图结构表示以及进行病原体预测等方面的实用价值。  

**代码获取**  
用于构建MetagenomicKG及其相关分析功能的源代码及技术细节均可在GitHub上获取：https://github.com/KoslickiLab/MetagenomicKG。本文中使用的数据，包括预构建文件和案例输入数据，均已存档在Zenodo平台上。

**摘要**

papers.title: Introducing non-enzymatic crosslinks into atomistic simulations of collagen fibrils
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Collagen fibrils are the primary load-bearing units of connective tissues. However, generating atomistic, simulation-ready models remains challenging due to collagen’s hierarchical organization and the diversity of its crosslinking network across tissues, ages, and metabolic states. Notably, non-enzymatic advanced glycation end-product (AGE) crosslinks—central to aging and diabetic complications—are largely absent from current atomistic fibril modelling workflows. Results Here, we present an extension of the ColBuilder framework to generate atomistic collagen fibril models that incorporate three representative AGE-derived crosslinks (glucosepane, pentosidine, and MOLD) alongside enzymatic crosslinks. Amber99-compatible parameters are provided and assessed against QM-optimized reference geometries using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. As proof-of-concept, we examine the mechanical response of single D-period collagen microfibrils featuring enzymatic-only, AGE-only, and mixed crosslink patterns in molecular dynamics simulations under force, and observe that AGE crosslinks differently impact the fibril structure compared to enzymatic crosslinks. The extension to ColBuilder can aid future structure-based research on collagen aging. Availability and implementation ColBuilder is available as an open-source Python command-line package at https://github.com/graeter-group/colbuilder

**软件可用性**  
ColBuilder作为一个开源的Python命令行工具包，目前可在以下链接获取：https://github.com/graeter-group/colbuilder

papers.title: CycleVI: Isolating cell cycle variation with an interpretable deep generative model
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Cell cycle progression is a dominant source of variation in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data, often obscuring other transcriptional signals of interest. Several methods have been developed to infer continuous cell cycle phase from transcriptomic data, but their estimates tend to be unstable when proliferation is intertwined with other biological processes or technical sources of heterogeneity. Results We present CycleVI, a deep generative model that disentangles cell cycle-driven variation from other signals in scRNA-seq data using a partitioned latent representation with a dedicated circular subspace. CycleVI accurately infers a continuous cell cycle phase, validated against orthogonal protein-level measurements, and yields a residual latent space free of cell cycle artefacts. This disentangled representation helps resolve biological processes intertwined with the cell cycle, clarifying hematopoietic differentiation and preserving drug-response signals better than standard cell cycle regression. By isolating cell cycle-related variation rather than removing it, CycleVI provides a principled framework for analysing cellular heterogeneity in proliferating systems. Availability CycleVI is available at www.github.com/jeuken/CycleVI , or through the ’cyclevi’ Python package

我们提出了CycleVI这一深度生成模型。该模型通过使用专门设计的循环子空间及分区的潜在表示方法，能够将scRNA-seq数据中由细胞周期变化所引起的变异与其他信号区分开来。
CycleVI能够准确推断出连续的细胞周期阶段，其结果通过正交的蛋白质水平检测方法得到了验证；同时，该方法所生成的残差潜在空间中不存在任何与细胞周期相关的干扰因素。

细胞周期的进展是单细胞RNA测序数据中变异性的主要来源，这种变性常常会掩盖其他重要的转录信号。虽然已经开发出多种方法从转录组数据中推断连续的细胞周期阶段，但当细胞增殖与其他生物学过程或技术性因素导致数据异质性时，这些方法的预测结果往往不够稳定。

all_papers.title: MetagenomicKG: a knowledge graph for metagenomic applications
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The sheer volume and variety of genomic content within microbial communities makes metagenomics a field rich in biomedical knowledge. To traverse these complex communities and their vast unknowns, metagenomic studies often depend on distinct reference databases, such as the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB), the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and the Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center (BV-BRC), for various analytical purposes. These databases are crucial for the genetic and functional annotation of microbial communities. Nevertheless, the inconsistent nomenclature or identifiers of these databases present challenges for effective integration, representation, and utilization. Knowledge graphs (KGs) offer an appropriate solution by organizing biological entities from different databases to standardized identifiers, allowing their interrelations to be captured into a cohesive network regardless of the naming conventions used in each source. The graph structure not only facilitates the unveiling of hidden patterns but also enriches our biological understanding with deeper insights. Despite KGs having shown potential in various biomedical fields, their application in metagenomics remains underexplored. Results We present MetagenomicKG, a novel knowledge graph specifically tailored for metagenomic analysis. MetagenomicKG integrates taxonomic, functional, and pathogenesis-related information on the human microbiome sourced from various databases, and further connects these with existing biomedical KGs to expand the biological network. Through various case studies involving the human microbiome, we demonstrate its utility in enabling hypothesis generation regarding the relationships between microbes and diseases, generating sample-specific graph embeddings, and providing robust pathogen prediction. all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
微生物群落中基因组信息的庞大数量与多样性使得宏基因组学成为了一个蕴含丰富生物医学知识的领域。为了研究这些复杂的微生物群落及其众多未知之处，宏基因组学研究通常需要依赖诸如基因组分类数据库（GTDB）、京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）以及细菌与病毒生物信息资源中心（BV-BRC）等参考数据库来进行各种分析工作。这些数据库对于对微生物群落的遗传特征与功能进行解析至关重要。然而，由于这些数据库在命名规则或标识符方面存在差异，因此它们的数据难以有效整合、呈现及利用。知识图谱通过将来自不同数据库的生物实体统一映射到标准化标识符上，使得这些信息能够被整合成一个连贯的网络结构，从而克服了上述问题。这种图结构不仅有助于揭示隐藏在数据背后的规律，还能帮助我们更深入地理解生物学现象。尽管知识图谱已在多个生物医学领域展现出巨大潜力，但其在宏基因组学中的应用仍亟待进一步探索。  

**结果**  
我们开发了一种专为宏基因组学分析设计的知识图谱工具——MetagenomicKG。该工具整合了来自多种数据库的人类微生物组的分类信息、功能数据以及与致病性相关的信息，并将这些数据与现有的生物医学知识图谱相连，从而构建出一个更为完善的生物学网络。通过多个涉及人类微生物组的案例研究，我们证明了MetagenomicKG在帮助建立微生物与疾病之间关系的假说、生成特定样本的图结构表示以及进行病原体预测等方面的实用价值。

all_papers.title: Introducing non-enzymatic crosslinks into atomistic simulations of collagen fibrils
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Collagen fibrils are the primary load-bearing units of connective tissues. However, generating atomistic, simulation-ready models remains challenging due to collagen’s hierarchical organization and the diversity of its crosslinking network across tissues, ages, and metabolic states. Notably, non-enzymatic advanced glycation end-product (AGE) crosslinks—central to aging and diabetic complications—are largely absent from current atomistic fibril modelling workflows. Results Here, we present an extension of the ColBuilder framework to generate atomistic collagen fibril models that incorporate three representative AGE-derived crosslinks (glucosepane, pentosidine, and MOLD) alongside enzymatic crosslinks. Amber99-compatible parameters are provided and assessed against QM-optimized reference geometries using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. As proof-of-concept, we examine the mechanical response of single D-period collagen microfibrils featuring enzymatic-only, AGE-only, and mixed crosslink patterns in molecular dynamics simulations under force, and observe that AGE crosslinks differently impact the fibril structure compared to enzymatic crosslinks. The extension to ColBuilder can aid future structure-based research on collagen aging. Availability and implementation ColBuilder is available as an open-source Python command-line package at https://github.com/graeter-group/colbuilder

**摘要与动机**  
胶原纤维是结缔组织中主要的承重单元。然而，由于胶原具有层次化的结构特征，且其交联网络在不同组织类型、年龄及代谢状态下存在显著差异，因此构建可用于原子尺度模拟的胶原模型仍然面临诸多挑战。尤其是那些与衰老过程及糖尿病并发症密切相关的非酶促糖基化终产物交联方式，在当前的原子级胶原纤维建模方法中几乎未被考虑。  

**研究结果**  
在本文中，我们对ColBuilder框架进行了扩展，使其能够生成包含三种典型AGE衍生交联类型（葡萄糖胺聚糖、戊糖苷及MOLD）的原子级胶原纤维模型，并同时保留酶促交联方式。我们提供了与Amber99软件兼容的参数设置，并通过全原子分子动力学模拟对这些参数的有效性进行了验证。作为概念验证，我们研究了在受力作用条件下，仅含有酶促交联、仅含有AGE衍生交联或同时包含这两种交联类型的胶原微纤维的力学响应，结果发现AGE衍生交联对胶原纤维结构的影响与酶促交联存在显著差异。这一扩展为未来基于结构机制的胶原老化研究提供了有力工具。

However, generating atomistic, simulation-ready models remains challenging due to collagen’s hierarchical organization and the diversity of its crosslinking network across tissues, ages, and metabolic states. Notably, non-enzymatic advanced glycation end-product (AGE) crosslinks—central to aging and diabetic complications—are largely absent from current atomistic fibril modelling workflows. Results Here, we present an extension of the ColBuilder framework to generate atomistic collagen fibril models that incorporate three representative AGE-derived crosslinks (glucosepane, pentosidine, and MOLD) alongside enzymatic crosslinks. Amber99-compatible parameters are provided and assessed against QM-optimized reference geometries using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. As proof-of-concept, we examine the mechanical response of single D-period collagen microfibrils featuring enzymatic-only, AGE-only, and mixed crosslink patterns in molecular dynamics simulations under force, and observe that AGE crosslinks differently impact the fibril structure compared to enzymatic crosslinks. The extension to ColBuilder can aid future structure-based research on collagen aging.

all_papers.title: CycleVI: Isolating cell cycle variation with an interpretable deep generative model
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Cell cycle progression is a dominant source of variation in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data, often obscuring other transcriptional signals of interest. Several methods have been developed to infer continuous cell cycle phase from transcriptomic data, but their estimates tend to be unstable when proliferation is intertwined with other biological processes or technical sources of heterogeneity. Results We present CycleVI, a deep generative model that disentangles cell cycle-driven variation from other signals in scRNA-seq data using a partitioned latent representation with a dedicated circular subspace. CycleVI accurately infers a continuous cell cycle phase, validated against orthogonal protein-level measurements, and yields a residual latent space free of cell cycle artefacts. This disentangled representation helps resolve biological processes intertwined with the cell cycle, clarifying hematopoietic differentiation and preserving drug-response signals better than standard cell cycle regression. By isolating cell cycle-related variation rather than removing it, CycleVI provides a principled framework for analysing cellular heterogeneity in proliferating systems. Availability CycleVI is available at www.github.com/jeuken/CycleVI , or through the ’cyclevi’ Python package

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
细胞周期的进展是单细胞RNA测序数据中变异性的主要来源，这种变性常常会掩盖其他重要的转录信号。虽然已经开发出多种方法从转录组数据中推断连续的细胞周期阶段，但当细胞增殖与其他生物学过程或技术性因素导致数据异质性时，这些方法的预测结果往往不够稳定。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了CycleVI这一深度生成模型。该模型通过使用具有专门设计环形子空间的分层潜在表示机制，将由细胞周期驱动的变异性与其他信号区分开来。CycleVI能够准确推断出连续的细胞周期阶段，并且其预测结果经过蛋白质水平测量的验证；此外，该模型还能生成一个不含细胞周期相关伪影的残差潜在空间。这种分离机制有助于厘清那些与细胞周期相互交织的生物学过程，从而更清晰地揭示造血细胞的分化过程，并比传统的细胞周期回归分析方法更好地保留药物反应相关的信号。由于CycleVI是针对细胞周期相关性变异进行分离而非直接去除这些变异，因此它为分析增殖系统中的细胞异质性提供了一个基于科学原理的分析框架。  

**获取方式**  
CycleVI模型可在以下地址获取：www.github.com/jeuken/CycleVI，或通过Python包“cyclevi”进行使用。
